mainEntity.name: How does drywall repair differ in historic Verde Valley homes around Jerome and Clarkdale?

acceptedAnswer.text: In regional communities like Jerome and Clarkdale, older homes with original lath-and-plaster walls or historic settling require specialized bonding and flexible compound choices. Traditional plaster moves differently than modern gypsum drywall, and historical walls often have subtle, hand-troweled undulations rather than uniform machine finishes. When patching drywall into historic plaster, contractors must mechanically secure loose lath, use setting-type compounds that bond to old plaster keys, and custom-trowel the texture to match irregular surfaces. Standard production spray textures often look out of place against historic, hand-worked architectural interiors found in these Verde Valley mining towns.
acceptedAnswer.description: Historic homes often feature plaster or aged framing, requiring setting-type compounds, mechanical stabilization, and custom hand-troweled texturing to match historic wall contours.
